chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: His first piano teachers, Fraley and the Italian neighbour
summary: Whaley recounts the candy-eating lady, Mr. Fraley and the Malden choir, an Italian teacher with a baton, and Walter Johnson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Just as a rehash again, because we separated these tapes, and I wanted to be sure that
we didn't miss anything -- what was your first teacher's name, or who first started you on piano?

I had a lady, I never knew her name, but she would sit there and eat candy, and I know I'd be making mistakes, so I told my mother, I told her -- "Look, she's eating candy all the time, and I make a whole lot of mistakes and she'll be saying that's very good" -- so then I got another teacher, a gentleman, his name was Fraley, and I remember him because he was a short, fat guy and he had a church choir up there in Malden, and he said he'd give me lessons if you'll come and sing, and he said he'd give me a tryout singing, and he found out I had a good voice, and I went up to the choir, had a robe, you know, one of these robes, black and white -- choirboy I was, and I used to sing up there all the time.
I'd go up there and he'd give me lessons, and he was very strict.
Did your mother play piano at all?

And across the street from where I lived, there was an Italian. They had two sons, I know, and he was a teacher, see -- and he was teaching, and I'd go over his house, and sit down and play the piano and he had a
great big long baton, see, as long as this cane, and when I'd make a bad note, he'd hit my hands, so I told my mother, "I ain't going over there any more, the man hit my hand!'

And she'd say, "You go over there." And this Walter Johnson, his father was a trumpet player, see, and we used to go over his house and play. I'd play -- I had a mandolin then, and I played mandolin there.
I had one of those things, too. And you say he was pretty good, you say, he was about the best around, you said, right?
Oh, Walter was terrific. He went out to California, see, and he died out there, but he went out there and played around.
